scope: Kale complete guide; first six Carrot and Parsnip Troubles conditions, excerpt only

consolidations.removed: Seed depth about 1/2 in.
Nursery rows 6 in. between seed rows
Final spacing About 18 in. between standard plants; allow more room for large varieties. Follow the packet for compact or baby-leaf crops.
consolidations.value: About 18 in. between standard plants; allow more room for large varieties. Follow the packet for compact or baby-leaf crops.

consolidations.removed: Use settled, fertile soil.
consolidations.replacement: Fertile, settled soil

consolidations.removed: Choose sun or light shade and good drainage; firm transplants securely.
consolidations.replacement: Drain well; firm transplants.

consolidations.removed: Keep plants steady.
consolidations.replacement: Keep plants steady

consolidations.removed: Water young plants and support loose stems against wind rock.
consolidations.replacement: Water; prevent wind rock.

consolidations.removed: Keep the spring crop growing.
consolidations.replacement: Spring feeding

consolidations.removed: Feed weak plants organically as growth resumes, only if needed.
consolidations.replacement: Feed only weak spring growth.

consolidations.removed: Choose sun or light shade and well-drained soil. Kale tolerates many soils, but fertile ground gives heavier crops.
consolidations.replacement: Choose sun or light shade and well-drained soil. Kale tolerates many soils but yields best in fertile ground.

consolidations.removed: Follow an early crop. Weed and improve the bed with mature compost where needed; let prepared soil settle or use a no-dig bed. Firm transplants without compacting wet ground. Lime only if a soil test indicates a need.
consolidations.replacement: Follow early crops; weed and add mature compost as needed. Use settled or no-dig soil. Firm transplants without compacting wet ground; lime only if a soil test indicates a need.

consolidations.removed: Weed carefully, water young plants and secure loose stems against wind rock. Avoid treading heavily on wet soil while tending the crop; check that tall plants remain firm after windy weather.
consolidations.replacement: Weed carefully and water young plants. Check and secure loose stems after windy weather, without treading heavily on wet soil.

consolidations.removed: Use supported insect-proof mesh where needed. Check beneath covers, keep them clear of leaves and secure bird protection. Leaf colour does not confer immunity.
consolidations.replacement: Support insect-proof mesh where needed and secure bird protection. Keep covers clear of leaves and check beneath them; leaf colour gives no immunity.

consolidations.removed: Use an organic liquid feed only if growth is weak as spring growth resumes; do not feed simply because it is March.
consolidations.replacement: Give an organic liquid feed only if spring growth is weak.

consolidations.removed: Pick a few tender outer leaves at a time, leaving the growing top and enough foliage for repeat crops. Avoid tough or yellow leaves.
consolidations.replacement: Pick tender outer leaves little and often. Leave the growing top and enough foliage for repeat crops; reject tough or yellow leaves.

consolidations.removed: Pick tender side shoots from late winter into spring. Removing a mature crown to encourage shoots is a separate harvest route, not a routine requirement for leaf picking. Take shoots while young and tender, typically about 4–5 in. long; timing varies with the variety and weather.
consolidations.replacement: Pick young, tender side shoots in late winter and spring, usually about 4–5 in. long; timing varies with variety and weather. Removing a mature crown encourages shoots; this is a separate method, not routine leaf picking.

consolidations.removed: Pick Red Russian leaves young; baby-leaf picking is not restricted to spring. Chop healthy finished stems before composting; follow disease guidance for affected roots. Cut finished healthy stems into short lengths, about 4–6 in., to help them break down.
consolidations.replacement: Pick Red Russian leaves young; baby-leaf harvest is not limited to spring. Chop healthy finished stems into short 4–6 in. pieces to help them compost; follow disease guidance for affected roots.

consolidations.removed: Sow thinly in a seed bed or modules. Cover the seed and thin crowded seedlings.
consolidations.replacement: Sow thinly in a seed bed or modules; cover and thin seedlings.

consolidations.removed: Move young plants with the lowest leaves just above the soil. Firm well and water in.
consolidations.replacement: Set lowest leaves just above soil; firm well and water in.

consolidations.removed: Final rows Usually 18–24 in. between rows of full-size plants; adjust for variety and growing method.
consolidations.replacement: Final rows Usually 18–24 in. apart for full-size plants; adjust for variety and method.

consolidations.removed: Choose spacing for your variety and growing method; larger plants need more room.
consolidations.replacement: Match spacing to variety and method; give larger plants more room.

consolidations.removed: Water nursery rows before lifting. June–early July sowings can follow early crops; transplant promptly when ready, often in July or early August. Allow time to establish and protect both early and late crops from pests.
consolidations.replacement: Water nursery rows before lifting. After early crops, sow June–early July; transplant promptly when ready, often July–early August. Allow establishment time and protect all crops from pests.
